capabilities: Analyze chapter notes in order to record threads, characters, and world rules
Flag contradictions in names, details, and world rules across chapters
Track foreshadowing from plant to payoff on a four-column board
Detect which later chapters an early edit affects and batch re-analyze them
Track reader knowledge separately from character knowledge across the timeline
extras: Analysis runs on the hosted Penseed service: note content is sent there when analyzed, and an optional (off by default) setting stores encrypted chapter text. Analysis consumes credits, though pricing is not stated in the README. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Board status syncs with the web app; full board editing happens there.
motivation: The author built it because most writing tools degrade on long books, re-reading everything per request, while Penseed reads each chapter once and remembers it, staying fast and cheap at 500+ chapters.
problem: Writing tools re-read the whole manuscript on every request, getting slow and forgetful as novels grow, and none track foreshadowing or what the reader knows at each point.

relations.evidence: Click the external-link icon on any card to open that foreshadowing's full detail view in the Penseed web app

summary: AI consistency companion for novelists that reads chapters in order, records plot threads, characters and world rules, and flags contradictions and dangling foreshadowing.
